note: Independent re-judge (not the author of the reactor unit). Section 4 read in rfc/full/rfc6996.txt: "Private Use ASNs MUST be removed from AS path attributes (including AS4_PATH if utilizing a four-octet AS number space) before being advertised to the global Internet."; ranges from Section 5 (64512 - 65534, 4200000000 - 4294967294 inclusive). Q1/Q2: TestRFC6996ExportRemovesPrivateUseASNsFromASPath drives runEgressPolicyChainASN4 toward an EBGP peer with an external member answering as-path remove "private" and asserts the exact UPDATE body: [64511 64512 65534 65535 4199999999 4200000000 4294967294 4294967295] becomes [64511 65535 4199999999 4294967295], so any off-by-one or widening of reactor isRFC6996PrivateASN at any of the four edges, or a dropped intent, turns it red; the AS4_PATH units assert the exact AS4_PATH set op ([64496 64497]) and zero ops for the four outside neighbours. Plugin units assert per edge that 64512, 65534, 4200000000, 4294967294 (and a private AS4_PATH behind AS_TRANS) draw exactly the remove intent, and that the four neighbours in AS_PATH and AS4_PATH draw accept. Q3: inputs isolate the range test. Q4: both attributes covered; for a two-octet EBGP destination the emitted AS4_PATH is the RFC 6793 transcode of the already rewritten AS_PATH (export chain on the collapsed four-octet route at reactor_api_forward.go, transcode in forward_body.go), which no tagged unit asserts end to end: implemented, stack proof for that destination still owed. Hand-written plugin breaks judged meaningful: >= 64512 to > 64512 is the real lower-edge off-by-one and the positive units observe it; <= 65534 to <= 65535 admits the reserved 65535 and the negative observes it; dropping isPrivateASN from the in-loop scan check (line 66) flags every ASN followed by a delimiter, coarse but it proves the negative depends on the range test. Reactor records are panic reverts, which prove reachability only; edge discrimination there rests on the exact-byte assertions read above. Claim wording: TestRFC6996StripsPrivateUseASN says 64512 draws the remove-private intent, but its body checks asPathFieldHasPrivateASN detection only; its sibling TestRFC6996RemovesPrivateUseASNsFromBothPathAttributes proves the intent.
